Subject: Kestrel inference discovery — technical confirmation and next steps

Avery / Diego —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick post-call recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured the technical highlights we discussed and the asks Kestrel called out. Please flag any corrections.

Summary of pain / goals
- Primary goal: real-time inference for customer-facing recommendations (N=3–5 requests/sec per region initially; plan to scale)
- Latency target: P95 < 220ms on short prompts (<=512 tokens); conversational P50 target ~90–110ms
- Throughput: steady state ~400 concurrent open sessions (KV cache active) across two regions in Q4; burst tolerance to 800 sessions for promotions
- Model requirements: Llama2-style 70B family (quantized int8q where possible), 8k context to start, plan to test 32k later
- Data controls: model call metadata must not leave customer VPC for Private deployment; logs retained for 90 days for debugging only

Deployment options we discussed
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood hosted with autoscale and cross-region routing — faster ramp but requires contractual data controls
- Dedicated reserved capacity: predictable throughput with dedicated GPU pools (recommended for Q4 ramp)
- Private (VPC): customer-managed VPC + Private control plane for regulated workloads (required if Kestrel needs full audit control)

Immediate next steps
1) Redwood to propose a conservative Dedicated sizing recommendation and a Private deployment checklist — due Tue 2028-07-25 (Ben + Marissa)
2) Kestrel to share representative prompt set and three sample session traces (anonymized) — due Thu 2028-07-27 (Avery)
3) Legal/Procurement intro for procurement questions & initial MSA review (Ben to loop legal contact)
4) Tech deep-dive scheduled: Tue 2028-07-26 10:00 PT (Ben, Marissa, Stephanie; Kestrel eng + infra)

Attachments: redwood-deploy-options.pdf (pdf) — recommended topologies; runbook-canary-template.md (md) — canary checklist

If that looks right I’ll kick off the sizing doc and send invites for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency: the P95 target you captured (<=220ms) is for user-facing single-turn recommendations. For multi-turn chat we’ll accept slightly higher P95 but want P50 preserved as our SLA baseline.
- Model: we expect to run a modified Llama-70B-cx we’ve been tuning. We’ll want to test both 8-bit quant and a 4-bit experimental profile — must confirm correctness/regression before any rollouts.
- Security: for the Private path we require KMS bindings + HSM key wrapping; we’ll detail in the questionnaire.

We’ll share the prompt set and session traces by Thu. For the deep-dive on Tue, can we add a short slot for telemetry — Diego will cover what we expect from runtime metrics and sampling.

Avery —

Appreciate the clarifications. Below is a short technical note ahead of Tue’s deep-dive (covers sizing, expected latency behavior, and topology options). Sharing now so your infra folks can review.

Technical notes (pre-deep-dive)
1) Sizing baseline (recommended conservative):
   - Model: 70B quant (int8/8q) — target performance profile measured on A100-like baseline
   - Dedicated pool: 6 x 80GB-GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100 or equivalent) per region for initial Q4 ramp. Assumes continuous batching + KV cache efficiency; expected steady throughput ~450 concurrent sessions with P95 ~200–260ms depending on prompt length
   - Burst capacity: allow autoscale up to +50% with pre-warmed pods for promotions (adds ~3 nodes per region)

2) Latency expectations and tradeoffs
   - Short prompts (<=512 tokens): P50 ~90–120ms, P95 ~180–260ms depending on quant profile and network egress
   - Long-context sessions (>=2k tokens) will see P50 increase; recommend session-level KV caching to keep interactive latency low
   - We recommend a mixed strategy: Dedicated for steady-state SLAs + Private for data governance-critical workloads. Hosted can be used for non-sensitive workloads and as fallback

3) Model compatibility & accuracy guardrails
   - We support quantized int8 and a beta 4-bit path; accuracy regressions are evaluated with your eval suite. Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts on your prompt set during canary
   - KV cache warm-up heuristics will be tuned during canary runs; provide sample session traces for best results

4) Topology options (what we’ll cover Tue)
   - Single-region Dedicated (fastest, lowest cross-region latency)
   - Dual-region Dedicated with Smart Routing (active-active, auto-failover) — recommended for higher availability
   - Private VPC deployment with Private control plane + KMS/HSM integration (adds ~2–3 day network/infra prep)

Attachments included: redwood-deploy-options.pdf (topology diagrams), kestrel-mhp-telemetry.csv (example telemetry schema). Also sharing runbook-canary-template.md as a starting canary checklist.

Proposed timeline
- Tue deep-dive (2028-07-26) — detailed topology and telemetry mapping
- Wed deliverable: sizing + cost band (Ben/Marissa)
- Thu Kestrel provides prompt set & traces

If that looks good I’ll have Marissa produce the sizing doc and we’ll confirm the invite.

Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
